severity_rationale: C4 Low/QA: 'State handling issues, spec deviations.' Direct spec deviation — feature spec item 6 states setWindowDuration should recompute per-second rate, but implementation only writes windowDuration. No direct funds-at-risk path: the monotonic-upward rate invariant means owner cannot slow emissions, but emissions still happen against an already-funded budget. The 'MEV rate-spike on next pull' is a timing redistribution among stakers, not external theft, and requires adversarial mempool observation plus favorable candidate arithmetic. Classified Low rather than Medium because no value is lost or stranded — all rewardBudget eventually emits; only the rate and timing are affected.
title: setWindowDuration does not recompute rewardRate or windowEnd, violating spec and creating a latent rate-spike MEV surface on next pull
description: setWindowDuration(newDuration) only updates the windowDuration storage variable (after _updatePool). It does not touch rewardRate or windowEnd. Two consequences follow from this single root cause: (1) Spec violation — feature spec item 6 in the submodule CLAUDE.md states: 'Changing the duration resets the remaining time to the new full duration and recomputes the per-second rate against the current balance.' The implementation violates this; emissions continue at the pre-existing rewardRate until the pre-existing windowEnd elapses. Because _applyAsymmetricWindow enforces a monotonic-upward rate, future refills can only raise the rate, never lower it, so the owner has no on-chain lever to slow emissions. (2) Latent rate-spike surface — after a shortening call, the effective schedule (rate * (windowEnd - now)) can diverge badly from rewardBudget / newWindowDuration. On the next nonzero _syncBudget pull, candidate = rewardBudget / shorterDuration is computed and can be >> rewardRate, triggering the reset branch and causing rate to jump with windowEnd reset to now + shorterDuration. Tests in NFTStakerPermissions.t.sol explicitly exercise this ('shorter window + 1 wei inflow rises rate').
attack_path:
Spec-violation path: 1) Owner funds B over default 540-day window. 2) Owner wants to slow emissions; calls setWindowDuration(10 years). 3) rewardRate and windowEnd unchanged — emissions continue at the higher rate until the original 540-day windowEnd. 4) Future refills cannot lower rate (monotonic invariant). Owner has no on-chain slow-down lever.

MEV path: 1) Owner calls setWindowDuration(shorter). No immediate state change to rate/windowEnd. 2) External observer watches the event. 3) Next hook pull produces any nonzero mint-debt; next stake/unstake/claim invokes _syncBudget. candidate = rewardBudget / shorterDuration >> rewardRate; reset branch fires; rate spikes; windowEnd = now + shorterDuration. 4) A staker who unstaked between step 1 and step 2 missed the spike. A staker who staked just before step 2 captures it. Timing-arbitrageable by anyone watching setWindowDuration events.
impact: Owner loses a documented governance control (cannot reduce emission rate) and users near a setWindowDuration event are exposed to MEV-style timing redistribution of rewards. The shortening case bakes in a latent rate spike that fires on the next nonzero pull, disadvantaging stakers who cannot watch chain state.
recommendation: Either (a) implement the spec behavior by atomically resetting rewardRate = rewardBudget / newDuration and windowEnd = now + newDuration inside setWindowDuration (breaks the monotonic-upward invariant, but this is the documented intent of the setter), or (b) trigger _applyAsymmetricWindow(0) with the scheduleExpired path from inside setWindowDuration so the rate and window update atomically, or (c) update the spec to document that setWindowDuration only affects subsequent refills. Option (a) or (b) also closes the MEV surface.

sanitization.rationale: Root cause is setWindowDuration in NFTStaker.sol (lines 145-151). Directly contradicts documented spec item 6 in submodule CLAUDE.md. Not a C4 universal-invalid pattern (not admin mistake: owner has no on-chain way to achieve documented behavior).
